items: Long-term steroids switch off the body's own cortisol
Never stop suddenly: taper, as ordered
NPO, vomiting, surgery or very sick? Ask for an IV steroid

memory_line: Steroids: never stop cold. NPO? Ask for IV.
caption_lesson:
🌙 Night shift, 2:30 AM. She's 70, on prednisone 10 mg every day for 2 years.
• Admitted with vomiting, made NPO (nothing by mouth)
• Her prednisone was held. Now: dizzy, weak, BP (blood pressure) 84/50

❌ 3 mistakes
1️⃣ Held her steroid, no call for an IV (intravenous) one
2️⃣ Called the low BP "just dehydrated"
3️⃣ Didn't report a low BP that fluids didn't fix
➡️ BP 68/40, heart rate 128, confused, low blood sugar. Rapid response.

💊 Prednisone (NEVER STOP COLD)
• Weeks to months of steroids switch off the body's own cortisol (adrenal suppression)
• Stop suddenly, or miss doses while sick, and there's not enough cortisol to hold the BP up
• That's an adrenal crisis

🚨 Adrenal crisis signs
• Low BP that fluids don't fix
• Vomiting, belly pain, weakness, confusion
• Low blood sugar

✅ The right move
• Never stop a long-term steroid suddenly. Taper, as ordered
• NPO, vomiting, surgery or very sick? Call for an IV steroid or a stress dose
• Crisis signs: call now. Hydrocortisone IV and fluids, as ordered

🧠 Steroids: never stop cold. NPO? Ask for IV.

rn_checks: Prednisone 10 mg daily for 2 years: high risk of HPA (hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal) axis suppression
NPO or vomiting on a long-term steroid: needs parenteral glucocorticoid (for example IV or IM hydrocortisone) as ordered; sick-day and stress dosing
Adrenal crisis: hypotension unresponsive to fluids, vomiting, abdominal pain, weakness, confusion, hypoglycemia; treat with hydrocortisone 100 mg IV and fluids as ordered (2024 ESE/ES; 2016 ES)
